purpose: Text-free opening illustration for both Whitepapers: guided mobile learning and prerequisite-based progress, not a screenshot or measured educational outcome.
prompt:
Use case: illustration-story.
Asset type: a polished editorial PNG illustration for the bilingual SkillPilot educational whitepaper, wide landscape about 16:9.
Primary request: make the idea immediately understandable and emotionally appealing: an upper-secondary learner is guided on her smartphone by a friendly AI learning coach through Mathematics and Physics, following a curriculum. Each skill she genuinely learns becomes a sound building block for the next, like constructing a solid house on strong foundations. The human learns; the phone guides.
Scene and composition: one coherent friendly comic scene, no panel grid. A young adult student, about 18 or 19, with dark curly hair and a teal sweater, at a simple study desk in the left foreground, concentrating with a small confident smile. Smartphone upright on a stand angled naturally toward her, and an open notebook on which she is actively drawing with a pencil. View from slightly behind and beside her shoulder so we can see part of the phone screen without turning it away from its user. Paper drawings are oriented toward the student, not unnaturally toward the viewer. The phone shows only an abstract chat bubble, a tiny smiling white-and-blue robot avatar and a short connected path of round steps: clearly an illustrative interface, not a screenshot.
Across the center and right is a clear imagined learning-house metaphor: a pleasing sturdy house being built from large interlocking rectangular skill blocks on a broad solid foundation, with stable horizontal layers. Two harmonious colors distinguish mathematics and physics; some blocks carry simple recognizable icons such as a coordinate curve, a geometric triangle, a pendulum and a sine wave. Completed lower blocks have small checkmarks; a single next block is subtly highlighted directly above supported completed blocks. The lightly outlined remaining upper courses and roof show the full intended house and the learning still ahead, rather than falsely claiming everything is completed. A curriculum blueprint beside its foundation and a restrained connected path from the phone to the next block explain guided sequencing. The house is an illustrative thought-picture, not literally miniature construction equipment on a desk.
Style: warm, approachable, abstract, clear hand-drawn comic illustration, confident rounded ink contours, gentle pastel teal/blue and warm amber accents, soft simple shading, airy ivory background, expressive human character. Compatible with a friendly educational comic, not photorealistic, not sterile vector icon art, not glossy 3D, not infantile. Readable silhouettes and very few details so it works on a phone and in print.
Text: NO words, NO letters, NO numbers, NO logos, NO watermarks. All factual product names and scope will be supplied as a typeset caption outside the image. No official seals, no graduation certificate, no instant mastery or automatic achievement, no robot doing the student's work. Keep the entire house, hands, smartphone and all important objects inside generous clean margins. Opaque continuous light background, no transparency, no black framing.

review.status: editorial AI-reviewed candidate; no human approval claimed
checks: Friendly abstract comic matches the established Whitepaper image language.
Phone and notebook face the learner; she actively works with a pencil.
Large supported blocks on a broad foundation; completed blocks differ from the single highlighted next goal and unfinished outline.
Mathematics and Physics are represented by schematic subject symbols, not a claimed exact dependency graph.
Phone UI is explicitly illustrative, not an actual Claude screenshot.
No private data, official seal, graduation promise or claim of automatically acquired mastery.
No raster editing or metadata stripping; generated PNG retained byte-for-byte.
review.disclosurePlacement: Shared italic notice beside Version/Project in the Whitepaper header
